article.headline: Joint models for 3D generation and control
article.lead: Recent methods enhance 3D generation and control through innovative architectures and frameworks. They improve performance in tasks like hand-object interaction, plant reconstruction, and spatial reasoning.

paragraphs.text: "Grasping-the-Future" predicts joint 3D hand-object motion using internet videos, achieving superior performance on 3D datasets through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching (1). Similarly, "Plant Orbiter" reconstructs 3D plant morphology from a single image, utilizing video diffusion to enhance accuracy and practicality, achieving the highest 3D F-score compared to existing methods (3). "Click3R" allows users to interactively correct geometric errors in stereo 3D reconstruction with minimal input, significantly reducing reconstruction error (9). InstantHMR enables real-time 3D human mesh recovery on mobile devices, achieving fast performance while maintaining competitive accuracy (10)."},{

What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching — The paper introduces the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which enhances the effectiveness of $v$-prediction in generative modeling by addressing bandwidth bottlenecks identified through patch-wise PCA analysis.

The paper introduces reComposer, an editable planning interface for image generation that enhances user control by decomposing creative decisions into distinct components such as subject, composition, and color palette.

The paper introduces SWAM, a novel approach to scaling World Action Models (WAM) that enhances language-video-action alignment through a comprehensive study of data supervision and model architecture.

The paper introduces $Σ$-LeWM, an enhancement to the LeWorldModel architecture for learning world models in robot control by incorporating two additional latent losses: a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor.
The paper introduces the Library of Hands (LoH), a novel training-free method that enhances world model performance by correcting the mapping from commands to actions without retraining the model.

How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time — The paper introduces MechEval, a framework for evaluating how many exposures a world model needs to learn mechanics in new environments, and presents WARC, a 35M-parameter vision transformer that updates all parameters after each transition.
The paper introduces Spatial Harness, a novel framework that enhances spatial reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs) by grounding it in executable world states using physics engines.

Beyond Modality Preference — The paper introduces a novel intervention technique for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that addresses the issue of modality conflict by controlling modality arbitration at inference time.
SkinMind introduces a novel multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that enhances dermatology AI by employing human-inspired graph probing for autonomous evidence seeking.

The paper introduces FewStepRL, a framework that adapts reinforcement learning (RL) objectives for fine-tuning few-step diffusion models, significantly reducing training costs associated with many-step samplers.
JoVox introduces a novel discrete flow matching framework for voxel generation that significantly enhances both fidelity and efficiency.
